input_topics: What is your relationship with mathematics?

Did you ever use AI to support your math learning in the last year? If yes, how was your experience?

How would you explain, step by step, how to find the stationary points of an equation y=f(x)?

I like chemistry and computer science more, but even those have math parts I struggle with. Now with my job, family, and hobbies like cooking and gardening, I avoid math. It's just not my thing, though I wish I was better at it.","Do you ever get anxious when thinking about mathematics?":"Yes, absolutely. Even thinking about math makes my heart race. Simple problems like balancing the budget for our family can make me sweat. With my high anxiety, I get overwhelmed easily. I'd rather knit or birdwatch to relax. Math feels like a big scary monster from school days that never left. I try to push it away, but it sneaks up.","Did you ever use AI to support your math learning in the last year? If yes, how was your experience?":"No, I haven't used AI for math learning. I'm too busy with full-time work, two kids, and chores. Maybe someday if it makes math less scary without much effort on my part.","How would you explain, step by step, how to solve a second order algebraic equation?":"A second-order equation is like ax² + bx + c = 0. First, ensure it's in that form. Then, calculate discriminant D = b² - 4ac. If D > 0, two real roots: x = [-b ± sqrt(D)] / (2a). If D=0, one root: x = -b/(2a). If D<0, complex roots. Basically, standardize data, compute covariance matrix, find eigenvalues/eigenvectors, pick top principal components. No, don't get anxious—it's just transforming data to simplify. But the math terrifies me; matrices and all. I'd use software like in computer science. Wish someone simple-fies it for beginners like us.","According to you, how can LLMs be used to innovate math learning in schools and universities?":"LLMs could make math fun and less scary by explaining simply, like a patient friend. For anxious folks like me, it reduces fear—try without embarrassment. Great for home learning too."},"reasoning_summary":"Responses reflect low education (avoids advanced math, simplistic explanations), high neuroticism (admits anxiety), low extraversion/conscientiousness (avoids effortful learning, prefers hobbies/family), high agreeableness (helpful, positive on AI), moderate openness (curious about CS/AI but limited), as a relatable Italian parent."}
